title: Sorghum grain, white, pearled, unenriched, dry, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Sorghum is the grain of the grass Sorghum bicolor, cultivated in warm regions worldwide. White pearled sorghum is polished to remove the outer hull, giving the grain a light color and a softer texture. It can be eaten raw, cooked, toasted, or used in porridges.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sorghum is one of the most drought‑tolerant cereals and is grown in areas with limited water supplies.
White pearled sorghum is popular in gluten‑free diets because it contains no gluten.
Sorghum has been a staple food in ancient African and Asian civilizations.
Pearled sorghum is high in starch, making it an excellent energy source.
Sorghum is also used to produce syrup, alcohol, and bio‑fuel.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Sorghum provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Sorghum is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds in sorghum help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sorghum.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytates can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting can mitigate this.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions may cause bloating and gas due to high fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sorghum can be boiled as a porridge, added to soups, salads, or baked goods, or ground into flour for gluten‑free baking. Rinse the dry grain and, if desired, soak it for 4–6 hours before cooking to improve digestibility.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry sorghum in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and flavor loss.
